top_results.section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > D. Total cost of ownership
top_results.text:
## D. Total cost of ownership

- [ ] Input/output tokens and cache-hit assumptions.
- [ ] Peak/off-peak prices, rate limits and minimum spend.
- [ ] GPU, storage, network and operations costs.
- [ ] Cost per successful task, not just price per million tokens.
- [ ] Retries, agent turns and tool costs.
- [ ] Budget limits and abnormal-usage alerts.

- **Resource ID:** 09

top_results.section: Claude API pricing and prompt caching > Enterprise selection questions
top_results.text:
## Enterprise selection questions

- How much input is repeated
- Can cache hits offset cache-write costs
- What invalidates cache breakpoints
- Does the estimate include input, output, cache and tool costs?

## 4. Cost requirements

- Estimate input, output, and cached-token usage from representative traffic.
- Include API charges, dedicated capacity, GPU rental or depreciation, storage, networking, and operations.
- Calculate cost per successful task, not only price per million tokens.
- Include retries, multi-step agent calls, and tool execution overhead.
- Define budget limits, quotas, and abnormal-usage alerts.

top_results.section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > C. Deployment and infrastructure
top_results.text:
## C. Deployment and infrastructure

- [ ] API hosting, dedicated deployment or fully private hosting.
- [ ] Region, data residency and network access.
- [ ] GPU type, VRAM, interconnect and compute budget.
- [ ] vLLM/SGLang/Transformers compatibility.
- [ ] Quantization quality regression.
- [ ] Parallelism, scaling, rollout and rollback.

## Reading notes

vLLM exposes HTTP endpoints compatible with several APIs, including OpenAI-style endpoints and Anthropic Messages. The documentation warns that API-key authentication does not protect every endpoint; production deployments need network controls and hardening.

top_results.section: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server > Enterprise selection questions
top_results.text:
## Enterprise selection questions

- Which APIs are required
- Are chat templates and tool-call formats compatible
- Are all exposed endpoints protected
- Are TLS, reverse proxy, rate limits and network isolation configured?

top_results.section: vLLM production metrics > Enterprise selection questions
top_results.text:
## Enterprise selection questions

- Are TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queue depth and KV-cache utilization monitored
- Can metrics be segmented by model and tenant
- Do alerts map to the SLA
- Is load testing documented?

# vLLM production metrics

- **Resource ID:** 14
- **Publisher:** vLLM Documentation
- **Official source:** https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/usage/metrics/
- **Purpose:** Design production monitoring, capacity planning and incident diagnosis.

## Reading notes

vLLM exposes Prometheus-style metrics through /metrics. Combine engine metrics with application success, timeout, cost, model version and user-feedback metrics for end-to-end observability.
